notes: Pro-style and premium residential ranges (gas, dual-fuel, induction) and built-in cooktops. NOT builder-grade freestanding ranges. Gas and induction are scored within the same framework but fuel_type is a key differentiator. Oven section scored WITH the range — cooktop-only products omit oven specs.

tier_anchors.notes: Wolf: Tier 1 consensus — dual-stacked sealed burners (500 BTU simmer to 20K sear), dual VertiCross convection, infrared broiler, Sub-Zero build quality, lowest service callbacks among pro ranges. BlueStar: Tier 1 for raw power — open burners up to 25K BTU, commercial heritage, Reading PA manufacturing, customization. Wolf edges on reliability/serviceability; BlueStar edges on max output. Yale + Town Appliance + installer consensus both Tier 1.

Thermador Pro Grand: BSH platform, Star burners, ExtraLow simmer, steam-assist oven. Strong features, competitive pricing vs Wolf, but pros rank just below Tier 1 on build quality. Thermador Freedom Induction: full-surface 48-element design, 63% more cooking area — top induction innovation. BSH reliability strong (1.7-4.9% induction service rate). Both strong Tier 2.

GE Café Gas: Yale 11.7% service rate — above 6.9% category average, higher than base GE (4.8%). Haier ownership. Selmer TN platform shared with Monogram/Profile. National service network is a strength. Bosch 800 Induction: BSH platform shares components with Thermador — 1.7% induction service rate (best in category). Punches above price point. Loses Thermador Freedom's full-surface innovation.

Samsung: cross-category service ecosystem problems carry over. No Yale gas range service data but pattern consistent. Control board reliability concerns. Contracted repair network. Dacor expected Samsung-sourced. Builder-grade competitors (base GE, Whirlpool, Amana, Frigidaire) also in this tier.
No calibration products. Reserved for brands with active safety recalls, no US service infrastructure, or documented structural defects.

quality.notes: Fuel type is a differentiator, not a quality hierarchy. Pro-style gas, dual-fuel, and induction are all premium. Standard gas slide-in = builder-grade positioning.

Wolf dual-stacked sealed (+2): two concentric flame rings, independent gas feeds, 500 BTU simmer to 20K sear. BlueStar open cast (+2): single-piece cast, up to 25K BTU, commercial heritage. Thermador Star (+1): 5-arm geometry. Standard sealed (0): commodity. Stamped aluminum (-1): builder-grade.

Thermador Freedom full-surface (+2): 48 individual elements, cookware anywhere. Flex/bridge (+1): zones that combine. Fixed premium (0): 4-5 discrete zones with boost. Fixed standard (-1): budget 4-zone.
Continuous heavy cast iron grates allow sliding between burners. Individual cast iron = standard premium. Porcelain-coated stamped = builder-grade.
Same as wall ovens. Wolf VertiCross, Miele TwinPower = dual fan + ring element (+2). True European single fan (+1). Fan-assisted (0). Standard thermal (-1). Cooktop-only products: N/A.
Wolf (+1, Fitchburg WI). BlueStar (+1, Reading PA). Miele (+1, Germany). BSH (0, multi-factory). GE/Haier (0). Samsung (0).

performance.notes: BlueStar 25K BTU is the benchmark. Wolf 20K. Thermador 18K. Standard 15K.
Wolf 500 BTU simmer via precision valve + orifice is the benchmark. Thermador ExtraLow competitive. Budget ranges often can't hold below 1000.
Thermador Freedom 4600W. Most premium induction 3700W. Budget under 3700W.
Same as wall ovens. Wolf VertiCross and Miele TwinPower top this metric.
Wolf infrared broiler is a genuine performance differentiator — faster, more even searing. Gas standard and electric are equivalent.
Induction inherently faster than gas. Among gas: open burners (BlueStar) fastest. Among induction: Thermador Freedom sub-2 min documented.

durability.notes: Yale gas range data: GE base 4.8%, LG 5.5%, GE Profile 10.1%, Café 11.7%. Category avg 6.9%. Induction: Bosch/BSH 1.7%, Thermador 4.9%, Gaggenau 0%. Induction generally more reliable than gas (fewer mechanical parts).

Igniters are the #1 gas range repair. Silicon nitride lasts 2-3x longer than silicon carbide. Electronic spark (Miele, some European) eliminates hot-surface igniter failure entirely. Induction ranges: N/A.
GE: owned national network. BSH/Whirlpool: widely stocked. Wolf/Sub-Zero: factory-certified (smaller but competent). Samsung: contracted, thin.
GE/Whirlpool: universal. BSH: widely stocked. Wolf/BlueStar: proprietary but available. Samsung: proprietary, thin availability.
Control board is the #2 range repair after igniters. Samsung has documented pattern failures across categories.

scoring_rules: Gas and induction scored within the same framework. Fuel type does NOT create an automatic tier advantage — a great gas range and a great induction cooktop can both be Tier 1.
For ranges: score the cooktop AND oven section together as one product. For cooktop-only products: omit oven specs, score cooktop only.
BSH Platform Rule: Bosch, Thermador, and Gaggenau share induction platform. Report must disclose. Thermador Freedom is genuinely differentiated hardware.
Wolf/Sub-Zero: factory-certified service network. Deep dive should confirm manufacturing location.
BlueStar: Reading PA manufacturing. Confirm in deep dive. Open burners = higher maintenance but higher performance.
GE Platform Rule: Monogram, Café, Profile, GE base share Selmer TN platform. Yale data shows GE base (4.8%) is MORE reliable than Café (11.7%) — deep dive must investigate why.
Samsung/Dacor: Dacor likely Samsung-sourced. Confirm in deep dive.
Igniters are the #1 gas range repair. Score igniter type explicitly.
Induction reliability is generally BETTER than gas (fewer mechanical parts). BSH induction 1.7% service rate vs 6.9% gas average.
Cross-category with wall ovens: if range oven section shares components with wall oven, mandatory platform disclosure in both reports.
Yale gas range data is available for GE, LG, GE Profile, Café. Wolf/BlueStar/Thermador service data: check deep dives.
